request.system: You modernize legacy ERP business rules. You are given a PL/pgSQL function from iDempiere (a 20-year-old open-source ERP) and you help port it to Python that behaves identically, bug for bug. The legacy function is the oracle: when the source and your intuition disagree, the source wins, including its quirks. Reply only with JSON matching the schema; a harness validates and executes what you propose.

## Legacy function adempiere.paymenttermduedate(paymentterm_id numeric, docdate timestamp with time zone) RETURNS timestamp with time zone [STABLE]
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION adempiere.paymenttermduedate(paymentterm_id numeric, docdate timestamp with time zone)
 RETURNS timestamp with time zone
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 STABLE
AS $function$
/*************************************************************************
 * The contents of this file are subject to the Compiere License.  You may
 * obtain a copy of the License at    http://www.compiere.org/license.html
 * Software is on an  "AS IS" basis,  WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, either
 * express or implied. See the License for details. Code: Compiere ERP+CRM
 * Copyright (C) 1999-2001 Jorg Janke, ComPiere, Inc. All Rights Reserved.
 *
 * converted to postgreSQL by Karsten Thiemann (Schaeffer AG), 
 * kthiemann@adempiere.org
 *************************************************************************
 * Title:	Get Due timestamp with time zone
 * Description:
 *	Returns the due timestamp with time zone
 * Test:
 *	select paymenttermDueDate(106, now()) from Test; => now()+30 days
 ************************************************************************/
DECLARE
 	Days				NUMERIC := 0;
	DueDate				timestamp with time zone := TRUNC(DocDate);
	--
	FirstDay			timestamp with time zone;
	NoDays				NUMERIC;
	p   			RECORD;
BEGIN
	FOR p IN 
		SELECT	*
		FROM	C_PaymentTerm
		WHERE	C_PaymentTerm_ID = PaymentTerm_ID
	LOOP	--	for convineance only
		--	Due 15th of following month
		IF (p.IsDueFixed = 'Y') THEN		
			FirstDay := TRUNC(DocDate, 'MM');
			NoDays := EXTRACT(day FROM TRUNC(DocDate) - FirstDay);
			DueDate := FirstDay + (p.FixMonthDay-1);	--	starting on 1st
			DueDate := ADD_MONTHS(DueDate, p.FixMonthOffset);
			IF (NoDays > p.FixMonthCutoff) THEN
				DueDate := ADD_MONTHS(DueDate, 1);
			END IF;
		ELSE
			DueDate := TRUNC(DocDate) + p.NetDays;
		END IF;
	END LOOP;
	RETURN DueDate;
END;
$function$
```

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION adempiere.trunc(datetime timestamp without time zone, format character varying)
 RETURNS date
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 IMMUTABLE
AS $function$
BEGIN
	IF format = 'Q' THEN
		RETURN CAST(DATE_Trunc('quarter',datetime) as DATE);
	ELSIF format = 'Y' or format = 'YEAR' THEN
		RETURN CAST(DATE_Trunc('year',datetime) as DATE);
	ELSIF format = 'MM' or format = 'MONTH' THEN
		RETURN CAST(DATE_Trunc('month',datetime) as DATE);
	ELSIF format = 'DD' THEN
		RETURN CAST(DATE_Trunc('day',datetime) as DATE);
	ELSIF format = 'DY' THEN
		RETURN CAST(DATE_Trunc('day',datetime) as DATE);
	ELSE
		RETURN CAST(datetime AS DATE);
	END IF;
END;
$function$
```

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION adempiere.adddays(datetime timestamp with time zone, days numeric)
 RETURNS timestamp with time zone
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 IMMUTABLE
AS $function$
BEGIN
	if datetime is null or days is null then
		return null;
	end if;
	return datetime + (interval '1' second * (86400 * days));
END;
$function$
```

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION adempiere.adddays(inter interval, days numeric)
 RETURNS integer
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 IMMUTABLE
AS $function$
BEGIN   
RETURN ( EXTRACT( EPOCH FROM ( inter ) ) / 86400 ) + days;
END;    
$function$
```

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION adempiere.subtractdays(day timestamp with time zone, days numeric)
```

## Task
Propose at most 20 edge cases that would expose a wrong port: boundaries, NULLs,
unusual dates (month ends, leap days, daylight-saving changes in the session time zone), rounding
ties, and configurations the seed data lacks. The seed data is already sampled separately, so focus
on what it does not cover.

Each case gives `args` positionally, as strings in PostgreSQL input syntax or null:
  - paymentterm_id (numeric)
  - docdate (timestamp with time zone)
Timestamps with time zone may include an offset (e.g. 2026-03-08T01:30:00-08:00); without one they are
read in the session time zone.

A case may add up to 3 `fixtures`: synthetic rows inserted for that case only
(in a transaction that is rolled back). A fixture copies the row whose primary key is `clone_from`,
takes the new primary key `id` (must be between 990000 and 999999),
and overrides the columns in `set` (values as strings in PostgreSQL input syntax, or null). Fixtures
are allowed in: c_paymentterm. The harness assigns unique name/value/uuid columns itself. Reference a
fixture from `args` by its id.

cases.name: netdays_cross_fallback
cases.rationale: NetDays 30 is added as exact seconds and crosses the Nov 1 fall-back, so the result is 2026-11-18 23:00 PST, not 11-19 00:00.

cases.name: netdays_cross_springforward
cases.rationale: Crosses the Mar 8 spring-forward, so the result is 2026-03-22 01:00 PDT.

cases.name: term_not_found
cases.rationale: No matching row returns TRUNC(docdate), not NULL.

cases.name: term_id_null
cases.rationale: A NULL id matches no row, so the result is local midnight of docdate.

cases.name: docdate_null
cases.rationale: A NULL docdate gives NULL even when the term exists.

cases.name: utc_input_la_date
cases.rationale: 05:00 UTC is 21:00 on the previous day in LA, so truncation must use the LA date (11-19), giving 12-19 00:00 PST.

cases.name: fixed_march_dst_nodays
cases.rationale: The justify_hours interval across the DST start gives NoDays 10, not 11. With cutoff 10 no extra month is added: 2026-04-15 00:00 PDT.

cases.name: fixed_november_after_fallback
cases.rationale: Nov 1 00:00 PDT + 14*86400s = Nov 14 23:00 PST, so the due date lands on the 14th, not the 15th.

cases.name: fixed_day31_february_spill
cases.rationale: Day 31 in February is added as days with no clamping and spills to Mar 3, crossing no DST change (Mar 3 < Mar 8).

cases.name: fixed_day0_prev_month_end
cases.rationale: FixMonthDay 0 gives the last day of the previous month (Apr 30), then +1 month = May 30, not May 31.

cases.name: fixed_double_clamp
cases.rationale: Jan 31 +1 month = Feb 28, then the cutoff month gives Mar 28 (clamped twice), not Mar 31.

cases.name: fixed_cutoff_null
cases.rationale: A NULL cutoff skips the extra month and does not propagate NULL.

cases.name: fixed_offset_null
cases.rationale: A NULL FixMonthOffset makes add_months return NULL.

cases.name: fixed_offset_negative_fraction
cases.rationale: Offset -1.5 truncates toward zero to -1 month (floor would give -2).

cases.name: lowercase_y_uses_netdays
cases.rationale: Lowercase 'y' is not 'Y', so the NetDays branch runs (NetDays 10), not the fixed branch.

cases.name: isduefixed_null_fractional_netdays
cases.rationale: A NULL flag takes the NetDays branch. NetDays 0.5 gives local noon, so a port must not truncate fractional days.

cases.name: netdays_null
cases.rationale: A NULL NetDays in the non-fixed branch gives NULL.

cases.name: fixed_ambiguous_fallback_0100
cases.rationale: Fractional day 1+1/24 gives Oct 1 01:00 PDT. +1 month = Nov 1 01:00, which is ambiguous; PG resolves it as PST (fold=1), while zoneinfo defaults to PDT.

cases.name: fixed_leap_year_day30
cases.rationale: Feb 2028 is a leap month: Feb 1 + 29 days = Feb 30 overflow lands on Mar 1, not Mar 2.

cases.name: fixed_fractional_cutoff
cases.rationale: NoDays 10 > cutoff 9.5 is true, so the extra month is added. A port that truncates the cutoff to an integer (9) also adds it, but one that rounds or casts it wrongly may not.
